## Changes
- **Simplify never removes a band the map needs.** Near a source that sits beside a building, thin inner bands were being merged into their neighbours, so a band could vanish from between two others and one contour line then stood for two levels (P2012 at a 4 m grid lost a band at 25 %). At any Simplify or Smoothing setting the highest band, and every band that lies between a higher and a lower one, is now still drawn. A lone speck that is lower than everything round it is still cleaned away. Display only: no calculated level changes.
- **The Simplify and Smoothing control responds at once.** After a drawing appears, AURIS draws the settings one move of the control away in the background (on maps of up to 300,000 points), so moving the control shows the new drawing without a wait.
- **A new drawing fades in over the old one** in the Editor and the Contours preview, instead of replacing it in one frame. Exports and images always take the finished drawing. Off with Reduce Motion, and on maps too large to paint twice a frame.
- **Results has one Calculate button.** It reads "Recalculate" when the levels shown are out of date, "Calculate all scenarios" when there are several scenarios, and "Calculate" otherwise. The out-of-date banner keeps its sentence and "What changed?"; while the button reads "Recalculate", "Calculate all scenarios" is under More.
- **Tables sort names with numbers in them in counting order**: "Building 8" before "Building 11", in the Results building groups and in every Inputs column.
- **ISO/TR 17534-3 cases are now also recorded on the screening formula projects use.** The TR was written for ISO 9613-2:1996, and AURIS's validation runs it that way (T01 to T18 within 0.5 dB). Run on the ISO 9613-2:2024 formula, T01 to T07 agree within 0.01 dB and T10 to T18 within 0.5 dB; T08 and T09 differ by up to 0.79 dB at 63 Hz and 125 Hz. The table is in `docs/validation/tr17534-3-on-2024-formula.md` and a test holds it. It is a record, not a pass: the TR has no control values for the 2024 formula, and a hand calculation from the 2024 text is still owed.
- **Two more regression scenes, modelled as the practice models them:** a padel club (four courts with their walls, set from the bundled measured court record, with a clubhouse, car park, acoustic fence and houses on two sides) and a school round a courtyard beside a road. Their receptor levels and grids are frozen, so any later change to them is caught.
- **Results shows a building by its name.** "8 Phillip Street", not "8 Phillip Street (BLD_006)". The id is added only where two buildings share a name; it still has its own column in the copied table and the Excel export.

## Bug fixes
- **Opening a padel project no longer freezes AURIS.** Once the Results tab had been opened, AURIS calculated the courts' maximum levels (LAFmax) on the interface thread every time Results refreshed after the model changed, and that included opening a project. On P2001 (five courts, ten receptors) the window did not respond for about 20 seconds. Maximum levels of area and line sources are now calculated in the background, as they already were for courts on "Worst case of all": the project opens at once and the maximum levels appear when they are ready. The levels themselves are unchanged.
- **Another project's maximum levels are never shown while the new project's are being calculated.** The columns stay empty until the new values arrive.
- **A dot no longer appears on the map in open ground (introduced in 0.95.0).** 0.95.0 kept every small band that was louder than its surroundings, which also kept specks of the interpolation that are not round any source (seen on P2003 at a 2 m grid). The loudest band is now kept where a source is, and a speck elsewhere is cleaned away as it was before 0.95.0.
- **Criterion fields in the padel and scheme assessment dialogs are no longer cut off at the bottom.** The value boxes ("50.0 dB", the LOAEL and SOAEL fields) were taller than their row.
- **Keyboard shortcut sheet: the key labels are drawn as pills again.** Their style rule was malformed, so Qt ignored it and logged a warning for each key.

## Changes
- **Simplify never removes the loudest band.** With Simplify at 100 %, the innermost ring round a source (the highest band on the map, where no calculated point falls inside it) was dropped as too small to matter, so the map could show a lower highest band than was calculated. A band that is louder than the band round it is now always kept. Other small bands are simplified as before.
- **3D View: receptor labels show names only when there are no current levels.** When nothing has been calculated for the model as it is now, every label read "REC_004 —". The labels now show the names alone, and the status line says once that levels need a calculation.
- **"SoundPLAN" sheet style: the north arrow sits in the bottom left-hand corner of the map, in grey**, as on SoundPLAN sheets.

## Bug fixes
- **The real-project check runs again.** AURIS's own check that opens every project in the practice's folder, calculates it and compares each receptor's level with the band drawn under it had been failing silently on every project since the noise-map rebuild (it read parts of the Contours tab that no longer exist, and hid the error). It is repaired and now reports its own failures.

## New features
- **Sheet styles are a gallery.** Contours › Sheet shows every built-in style as a small picture of the sheet it makes: where the logo sits, whether the details are in cards, the heading colour, the side panel or the on-map key. Click one to apply it; the one in use is ringed. The pictures are drawn from the style definitions themselves, and their headings take your company colour when it is set to be used on sheets. The dropdown above stays for styles you have saved in the project.

## Bug fixes
- **A possible crash when changing page in Contours or Settings is fixed.** The page cross-fade added in 0.93.0 created and destroyed a small Qt object on every change; building the next one could crash the app (in tests, about one run in eight of the Contours suite). The cross-fade now reuses one overlay and creates nothing per change; 24 repeat runs of the same tests had no crash.
- **Settings: the summary line no longer fails intermittently when it restyles** (a PySide fault that occasionally returned the wrong object for the label's style).

## Changes
- **Road bends are drawn as curves.** A road is entered as straight runs between nodes, so each bend had a point on the outside and a notch on the inside. The Editor, the Contours preview and exported sheets now draw every bend as an arc that meets both runs smoothly, with the edge lines and lane markings following it. This is drawing only: CRTN and ISO 9613-2 still calculate from the nodes you entered, so no level changes. Roads with a varying cross-section, and the 3D View, are drawn as before.
- **Noise maps: rings round a point source stay round on a coarse grid.** Where a map is dominated by point sources on open ground, the drawing now interpolates the levels after taking out each source's own fall-off with distance, and puts it back exactly. On the reference case the largest error at a 4 m grid falls from 5.9 dB to 0.5 dB and the band edges move from up to 0.9 m out to under 0.1 m. The calculated points are untouched and receptor levels do not change. AURIS checks, on the calculated points themselves, that this predicts them better than plain interpolation, and uses it only where it does: on the reference projects with buildings and screens it is not used, and their maps are drawn exactly as in 0.92.0.
- **Dark mode: the north arrow and scale bar choose their ink by what is under them.** Light on the dark canvas, black with a white halo over a basemap, each decided separately.
- **Pages cross-fade.** Switching between Calculate, Style and Sheet in Contours, and between pages in Settings, now fades the old page out over the new one in about a fifth of a second. The new page is live from the first frame. With Reduce Motion on, pages swap at once as before.

## Bug fixes
- **Dark mode: the plan no longer reports "Something didn't work" over a tiled basemap.** In 0.92.0, with the interface dark and a tiled basemap (OS mapping, satellite imagery) on the plan, every repaint raised an error and the north arrow and scale bar were not drawn. Fixed; the plan paints normally.
- **Dark mode: switches that are off are dark.** The animated switches (for example Intermittency and Other characteristics in Results › BS 4142) still showed a pale track that read as "on".

## New features
- **Roof noise maps in the 3D View.** Display › Building façades has a "Roofs" switch (off by default). Turned on, each building that receives façade results also gets a level map over its roof, calculated 1.5 m above the roof (a person standing on it) and screened by the roof edge as the standard requires. It follows "Show as": the flowing map with Contours, or one colour for the whole roof (majority or highest) with Per façade and Per floor. Hovering over a roof reads its level. Turning it on recalculates the façades, because it adds calculation points; the façade levels themselves do not change.
- **Sheet style "NoiseMap 5".** A sheet laid out like a NoiseMap 5 plot: no side panel, a boxed "Contour Scale (dB)" key with the limits printed as "67.5-70.0", and a ruled table (Model, Scenario, Contour Result, Period, Method) in the bottom right-hand corner of the map, in Courier New.
- **Company colour and font.** Settings › Organisation has "Colour", "Font" and "Use on sheets" for each company. With "Use on sheets" on, the sheets of that company's projects take its colour for their headings and its font for their text, so figures match the rest of your reports. The font list starts with the faces report templates usually use, then every font on this Mac. The SoundPLAN and NoiseMap 5 styles keep their own font and take only the colour.

## Changes
- **Dark mode has been rebuilt.** The surfaces are darker and neutral (the old set read as dark green), with clear steps between the window, panels, cards and fields; secondary text is lighter. The selected option of every segmented control is now plainly lighter than its track (it was darker, so "Light | Dark" barely showed which was chosen), and a switch that is off no longer looks like a white, switched-on pill.
- **The plan is dark in dark mode.** The Editor canvas and the Contours tab's Editor view use a dark canvas with a quiet grid; the north arrow and scale bar switch to light ink when there is no basemap under them. Every export, copy and sheet is still the light plan, whatever the mode on screen. The Sheet view stays white paper, because it shows exactly what will be exported.
- **Window title bars follow dark mode.** Settings and other windows drew a dark title on a dark bar; they now take the system's dark title bar.
- **The "SoundPLAN" sheet style is redrawn from a SoundPLAN sheet.** A thin dark frame round the map and the panel, the project number and name as the green title, "Signs and symbols", "Levels in dB(A)" as touching swatches from quiet to loud with the limits in columns ("15  -  20", "<  15", ">=  85"), the scale as "1 : N" over a segmented bar in the panel (not on the map), and the logo across the foot. The co-ordinate neatline is turned off, as SoundPLAN sheets have none.
- **Contours: three pages, not four.** Calculate, Style and Sheet. The Map page is gone: the basemap layers are on the toolbar above the map, to the left of "View"; "Objects" (building name size, colour by level) is on Style; "Save map layers as a basemap…" is under Style › Fill. Site outlines are drawn with the Editor's outline tool; Sheet has one "Site outlines" switch for showing them.
- **Drawing: the segment being placed runs from the outline's colour into teal**, so the placed outline flows into the part still to place.
- **Snapping to an edge lights the edge at the pointer** and fades away along it on either side, in place of the whole edge turning teal.

## Changes
- **Façades in 3D: contours, one colour per façade, or one colour per floor.** The façade panel now starts with "Show as": Contours (the calculated levels flowing across each wall), Per façade (each wall one colour) or Per floor (each storey of each wall one colour, from the building's storey heights).
- **A flat façade colour can be the majority band or the highest level.** "Colour from › Majority" uses the median level of the wall or storey, so a sliver of a higher band no longer recolours the whole face. "Highest" uses the worst level, as assessments do. The legend title says which is shown ("Majority incident level per storey"). Assessment tables always use the highest level, whatever is drawn.
- **Façades can use their own palette.** "Colours" offers every built-in palette (SoundPLAN, CadnaA, ProPG, AVO Day/Night, and the rest) or "Same as the noise map". The band edges stay the noise map's, so a wall and the ground beside it are classified alike.
- These are display choices: none of them needs a recalculation or changes a calculated level. Older 3D views open as before (Storeys becomes Per floor, Façade map becomes Contours).
- **North arrow types.** Contours › Sheet has "North arrow type": the AURIS compass, an arrow with N beneath it, a split needle, or a circle with an arrowhead. The choice is saved with the sheet and used in the preview and every export.
- **Sheet style "Logo card".** The logo sits in its own rounded card, with the same margins and corners as the cards below it.
- **Sheet style "SoundPLAN".** One click gives a SoundPLAN-style sheet: a grey side panel with green headings ("Signs and symbols", "Levels in dB(A)"), a stacked square colour key from quiet to loud, your organisation's logo as a block at the foot of the panel, Arial Narrow, the plain north arrow, and SoundPLAN's noise-map colours.
- **Palette "SoundPLAN noise map (15-85 dB)".** SoundPLAN's sixteen-colour 5 dB scale, available for noise maps and façades.
- **More fonts for the sheet's side panel.** Arial Narrow, Arial, Helvetica Neue and Calibri join Exo 2 (a font that is not installed falls back to a similar one).
- **The logo can sit at the foot of the side panel.** Put "Logo" last in Sheet › Detailed layout › Section order.

## Bug fixes
- **Results: the BS 4142 and BS 5228 side panels no longer squash.** In a window about 900 px high their fields and buttons were crushed to a few pixels and overlapped. Both panels now scroll, as Residential does.
- **Results: no "calculated" line under the out-of-date banner.** The footer said "Exact receptor results calculated." directly beneath "These levels are out of date". It now stays silent while the levels are out of date.
- **Results: the BS 4142 background labels are no longer clipped** ("Background, day", "Background, night", "Background, hours").

## Changes
- **Buildings can no longer be dragged taller or shorter in the 3D View.** Pulling a roof changed the building height, a calculation input, far too easily by accident. Height is set in the Inspector. Point sources, receptors and area sources still drag in 3D.
- **Building names sit inside the building.** On L-shaped, U-shaped and courtyard buildings the name was placed at the centre of the bounding box, which is beside or outside a wall. It now sits in the widest part of the building's body. Simple shapes keep their name in the middle.
- **3D receptor labels can show every period.** The Labels menu in the 3D View has "Levels: the period shown" and "Levels: all periods". With all periods, a label reads "Day 51.7 · Night 44.2 dB", and a receptor stack shows each period's range. A period with no current result shows a dash: out-of-date levels are never shown.

## Changes
- **Editing a road's night traffic says which period the previews show.** Receptor previews follow the Period selector. While it is on Day, the night inputs change nothing on the plan, which looked like a fault. The Inspector now shows "Receptor previews show Day. Show Night levels" under the night inputs; click it to switch the Period to Night.
- **Rename a basemap.** Open the layer's style popover and click the name beside "Layer A" or "Layer B". Enter keeps the new name, Esc cancels, and Undo restores the old one.
- **Realign a basemap after import.** For drawings, clipboard images and PDF pages, the popover has "Realign to the model…". It reopens the alignment used at import, so you can line the image up with the model and your other basemaps. The image, name, layer and style are kept; one Undo step. Map imports are georeferenced and keep their east/north offset instead.
- **Fill opacity is a slider.** Contours › Style › Fill: drag, scroll, or double-click to type a value.
- **Report basis says exactly what the validation covers.** The ISO/TR 17534-3 test cases were written for ISO 9613-2:1996, so AURIS runs them with the 1996 screening formula and the 2024 Kmet. The "Software validation" line and the report limitations now say so, and say that the TR does not test the 2024 screening formula used for the project. No calculated level changes.

## Bug fixes
- **"Choose from library" in the Inspector listed no AURIS records.** Since 0.55 the Inspector looked for the bundled library in a folder that does not exist, so only your own records appeared. All 484 bundled records are back. Every route to the library now uses one path.
- **Results no longer shows blank levels.** A receptor or floor added after a run was calculated has no level in that run. Its cell was empty; it now shows a dash, and its tooltip says to recalculate.
- **"Traffic flow must be positive" no longer stops a calculation.** A road with no traffic in a period (a night flow of 0 % of the 18-hour flow, or an 18-hour flow of 0) stopped every receptor with an error. No vehicles means no road noise: the road is now left out of that period, the calculation names it, and the other sources are calculated. Levels are unchanged wherever a calculation already ran.

## Changes
- **Contours: the grid is first, and always in view.** The four pages are now Calculate, Style, Map and Sheet. Calculate opens with a Grid card: spacing, height, margin and accuracy (Exact or Draft, until now only in Settings). A summary such as "1 m grid · 1.5 m high · Exact" sits above Update Grid on every page; click it to change the grid. Changing accuracy now marks the map out of date, as the other grid inputs do.
- **Contours: simpler, calmer pages.** Each section is a soft card instead of a list divided by hairlines. Source switches show only the source types in the model (no more "Points 0"). Receptor levels fold away under the result picker, and less used line options (black lines, minor isolines, label colours) sit under "More line and label options". The height note reads plainly ("The map is 1.50 m above ground; receptors are at 1.50–4.50 m…"), and it is amber only when the heights differ. With one scenario, the result tile names its period instead of showing a lone dot.
- **The 3D View stops drawing when nothing moves.** A still view used to be redrawn 24 times a second for as long as the 3D View was open. It now draws for 2.5 s after any change (camera, scene, lighting, size, quality), so smoothing and shading settle, and then rests until the next change.
- **Each area source level is shown once.** "Derived" now says how the level was given (for example "Broadband input · 500 Hz attenuation estimate; no measured spectrum."). The levels appear only under "Resulting sound power". A vertical pane's extent reads "2 nodes along the wall", because its Length and Area are shown just below.

## Bug fixes
- **The editor could crash after a building was moved and then deleted.** Moving, rotating or reshaping a building left it listed under its old position in the plan's drawing index. Deleting it, undoing or reloading then left a dangling entry, and the next redraw over the old position crashed AURIS (0.87.0 crash report, 12 Nov). Removed buildings, roads, line sources and outlines are now kept until the index has been rebuilt. On a 5,000-building model this costs about 30 ms after a deletion.
- **Padel LAFmax origins were drawn from a background thread.** When a court was selected, its LAFmax origin glyphs were added to the plan by the calculation thread, not the interface thread. This could leave the plan without glyphs, and it risked a crash like the one above. They are now always drawn on the interface thread. The levels are unchanged.
- **Courtyards are open air in ISO 9613-2 calculations.** The noise map always calculated grid points in a building's courtyard. The ISO 9613-2 engine, however, saw only the building's outer outline, so those points were treated as inside a solid block, under its roof. A courtyard building is now calculated the same way as the same block drawn as separate buildings around the courtyard. Courtyard walls now screen and reflect, and the building still screens as one object.
  - **Calculated levels change in courtyards only.** On the projects with courtyards: P1976a Hangar 4, 11 to 18 dB lower in the courtyard; P2013 Liquid Swords, 1.6 to 5.0 dB lower at three of the five courtyard centres (the other two are unchanged, because sound cannot reach them in either case). Receptor levels are unchanged on every project, and grid points outside buildings change by at most 0.0002 dB. The release gate's golden results are unchanged.
  - The pre-run check no longer reports a receptor or source in a courtyard as "inside a building".
  - CRTN already treated courtyards as open air. Rail (CRN) levels are unchanged and need no change: CRN screens with the building wall nearest the track, which is the same with or without a courtyard.
- **A building group could stop screening sideways.** When touching buildings are joined into one screening object, the outline could keep two corners a rounding error apart. The engine's inside test then treated the whole object as empty, so a sideways (lateral) path could run straight through it. In the case found, the screening fell from 20 dB to 1.8 dB. Repeated corners are now removed, and the test ignores zero-length edges. No golden result changed.

## New features
- **Smart snapping with Shift.** While drawing, hold Shift to snap to corners, edges, midpoints, intersections and the first point of the shape. Guides show perpendicular, parallel and aligned positions, and the usual angle steps still apply. A small label beside the pointer names the snap, for example "Corner" or "Aligned · 90°", with the length and bearing. Measure, Road and Railway snap too. A Shift-click on open ground still starts a roundabout.
- **Vertical area sources: type the base and height, or an area.**
  - The Inspector shows Base above ground and Height as the two fields you type into, with Top shown underneath (for example "Top 2.50 m above ground"), so you can check it against the eaves.
  - Area sits beside the pane's Length. Typing an area sets the height from the drawn length, and the pane keeps that area if you later change its length.
  - Changing the base moves the pane and keeps its height.
  - After a change of size, a short note gives the level that was held and the one that changed, for example "LwA per m² held at 72.0 dB; total 82.8 dB".
  - The per-node table is under "Vary along the wall" and opens by itself on a pane whose heights differ.
  - Tool defaults use the same fields, with an optional Area that sets each new pane's height from its drawn length.

## Changes
- **Faster shaped contours.** The shape stage now works on one shared network. Drawings are identical, and changing the shape on the busiest maps takes about 0.4 s instead of 0.6 s.
- **Shadow edges only where the grid can show them.** A building now cuts a shadow edge into the contours only where its shadow reaches about one grid spacing across the map. Small, distant buildings no longer cut thin wedges that the grid cannot resolve. Calculated levels are unchanged.
- **One set of names for vertical panes.** Every figure in the Inspector, including the per-node table, shows two decimal places. The 3D view's pane panel uses the same names as the Inspector: Base above ground, Height and Length.
- **Known limitations:** shaped contours on the very busiest maps (for example 32,000 points with many bands) can still take just over a second to draw from scratch.

## Bug fixes
- **Courtyards of imported buildings look solid in 3D.** The walls around courtyards and other cut-outs faced into the building, so they were not drawn and you could see straight through. They now face the courtyard. This changes the drawing only; calculated levels are unchanged.
- **Shaped contours keep every point in its own band.** In rare cases a shaped style could draw a calculated point inside the neighbouring band. The cause is fixed and a new check covers it.

## Changes
- **The editor stays responsive with captured basemaps.** Basemap images were decoded in a way that held up the whole window, for up to half a second when switching basemap on P2013. They now decode truly in the background (P2013: 502 ms down to 175 ms when switching).
- **Hovering, clicking and dragging no longer scan every building.** The plan's spatial index now spreads over the model instead of a fixed 100 km area. On P2013 the longest pause while hovering fell from 27 ms to 10 ms, and while panning from 34 ms to 21 ms; selecting a building is quicker too.
- **Smoother panning and zooming.** The scale bar is drawn once and reused, grid lines are drawn more cheaply with identical pixels, and an idle progress indicator no longer ticks in the background.

## Bug fixes
- **A building's outline no longer stops where it shares a wall.** On a wall shared with a neighbour, the more prominent style is drawn: selected or being edited, then a building with its own colour or style, then a plain building. A red-outlined building now shows its outline all the way round, on screen, on the Sheet and in exports.

## Changes
- **Esc steps back one point while drawing.** Esc now removes the last point placed, as Backspace does. A stray Esc no longer throws away every point of a building, barrier, road or outline in progress.
  - Shift+Esc clears the whole shape.
  - With no points left, Esc returns to Select as before.
  - The sheet's outline tool works the same way.
- **The Sheet view keeps up with the drawing.** On very fine grids the sheet waited about 1.5 s after a new drawing was ready before showing it. It now shows it within about a tenth of a second (P2012 at 0.125 m, 447,000 points).
- **No pauses when the sheet refreshes on Retina screens.** The sheet is now drawn in several short steps, so the window is never held for more than about 35 ms. The result is still identical, pixel for pixel, to the exported sheet.

## Changes
- **Contours draw the same however the model sits.** A map now draws identically when the model is moved to national-grid coordinates, turned or mirrored. Five orientation-dependent steps in the drawing were fixed, so lines and bands may move slightly on some maps, typically a fraction of a square metre per band.
  - **Wrong levels on some lines:** a contour line lying wholly inside a building or a no-data area dropped its line but not its level, so the lines after it carried the wrong level (a 50 dB line could be drawn as 45).
  - **Thin slivers:** these took their band from a point chosen in an orientation-dependent way.
  - **Shadow edges:** two cases in finding them depended on the frame.
- **Long curves stay curved at high Smoothing.** At linked 75–100 %, long outer contours no longer flatten into straight chords. Simplify at 100 % with Smoothing off is unchanged.
- **Cancelling a drawing takes effect at once,** within a twentieth of a second, even on very dense maps.
- **The first contour drawing after installing is quick.** Every drawing kernel is now prepared when the app is built, not on your Mac.
- **Contour calculations keep to their time limit.** A calculation given a time limit now stops on time and releases its workers; before, a large grid could run on for minutes.
- **Calculation workers no longer grow in memory.** Caches that were almost never reused grew by about 3 MB per receiver; on a 2,200-receiver grid each worker now stays near 540 MB instead of growing to 1.9 GB. Results and speed are unchanged.
- **The old contour code has been removed.** About 65,000 lines of the previous drawing and hidden-refinement code are gone; nothing used them any more. Calculated levels are unchanged.
- **Known limitations:**
  - **Speed on the busiest maps:** shaped contours on the busiest maps (for example 32,000 points with many bands) take about 1.2 s to draw; a faster shape stage follows in 0.86.1.
  - **Sheet view on very fine grids:** the Sheet view can take a few seconds to show a new shape on very fine grids (0.125 m and finer).

## Bug fixes
- **Validation presets open with their own receptor IDs again.** 0.85.1 renumbered the receptors of the built-in, read-only validation projects when they were opened. Read-only projects are no longer changed on open.
- **Bands no longer cross inside other bands at Simplify 100 %.** A rare case could leave neighbouring bands overlapping where a simplified line dragged a collapsed neighbour with it.

## Changes
- **Every Simplify and Smoothing setting now looks right.**
  - **Linked settings:** moving the linked control from 0 to 100 % now goes evenly from accurate contours to fluid curves. Linked 50 % is no longer more angular than either end: a single awkward line used to make the whole drawing fall back to its simplified, straight-edged form.
  - **Smoothing and Simplify together:** Smoothing keeps pace with Simplify, so any corner Simplify makes is rounded whenever Smoothing is on.
  - **Simplify alone:** Simplify at 100 % with Smoothing off stays plainly geometric.
- **Shadow edges stay straight and in place.** Where buildings or barriers start to screen a source, the level really does step, so that line never bends or moves. Where contours meet it, the corners round off more as Smoothing rises.
- **The Objects key names things the way you would.**
  - **One object:** a single point source, line source, area source, receptor, road, railway, barrier or parking lot shows its own name, for example "Air Source Heat Pump", or else the singular "Point Source".
  - **Several objects:** they show a name they share ("ASHP" for ASHP 1 and ASHP 2), or else the plural with a count ("Point Sources (3)").
  - **Generated names:** IDs such as SRC_001 are never shown as names.

## Bug fixes
- **Receptor IDs stay in step with their numbers.** Turning off a receptor stack left a gap in the IDs: on P2012, receptors numbered 1 and 2 on the plan were REC_001 and REC_003 in results. Turning a stack off now renumbers like any delete, and a project saved with gaps opens with consecutive IDs.
  - Default-style names follow the new IDs; names you gave your receptors stay.
  - Per-receptor inputs move with their receptor.
  - Results are recalculated after the IDs change.
- **Contour bands no longer reach inside buildings at shaped settings.** Simplify could cut a corner across a building, so neighbouring bands overlapped inside it (P1949, P1986, P2001). The building hid this on screen, but it reached GIS exports.
- **A window-styling error no longer appears in the error log.** AURIS checks the windows' native styling every tenth of a second, and it could stop on an object that was not a window.

## New features
- **Noise maps are drawn by a new engine, built from the ground up.** Calculate now solves the grid and nothing else. Drawing the map is a separate, fast step that never calculates, and it runs in the background so the window never waits:
  - **The calculated grid shows straight away.** The contours follow, typically within a second.
  - **Shape changes redraw quickly.** Simplify and Smoothing take about half a second or less.
  - **View-only changes repaint at once.** Colours, opacity, lines, labels and blend start no job.
  - **Drawing never stalls.** Switching style or cancelling never leaves the map blank: the last drawing stays until the new one arrives. On P2012 (0.5 m grid) switching to smoothed contours used to sit at 97 % for minutes while it made hidden extra calculations. It now draws in under a second.
- **Contours are smooth at any grid spacing, with sharp shadow edges.**
  - **Interpolation.** Bands and lines are drawn from one interpolated field that never overshoots the calculated levels.
  - **Walls and holes.** A level is never interpolated through a wall, and buildings are exact holes. There is no staircase, and no white gaps round buildings on coarse grids.
  - **Shadow edges.** Behind buildings and barriers they are found from the geometry, kept only where the calculated grid shows the step, and drawn as clean straight wedges.
  - **Accuracy.** Measured against exact solves at 0.125 m, the drawing is two to four times closer to the true field than plain interpolation. On P2012 the 95th-percentile error is 0.03 dB on a 0.5 m grid.
- **Simplify and Smoothing apply to every band boundary.**
  - **Simplify** makes them geometric, with straight runs and corners; at 100 % it is plainly geometric.
  - **Smoothing** then turns them into curves.
  - **Linked or separate.** The two controls are linked by default and can be split.
  - **Scale-free.** They behave the same on a 50 m site and a 5 km map.
  - **Bounded.** At 100 % a line may move until the field under it differs by half a band step; walls and the map edge never move.
  - **Receptors stay in their band.** Every receptor stays in the band of its own level at every setting.
- **SVG and PDF exports carry true curves.** Smoothed contours are written as cubic Bézier curves, so they edit cleanly in drawing software. Each boundary is fitted once, so neighbouring bands cannot gap. DXF, GeoPackage and GeoJSON keep dense polylines, which every CAD and GIS package reads reliably.
- **dB labels follow the lines.** Labels sit on straight-enough stretches of each line, upright and with a halo, and the line is cut beneath each label. They avoid each other, receptor names and the legend, and stay put when you pan.
- **One drawing everywhere.** The plan view, Sheet, PNG, PDF and SVG exports, GIS export, the 3D view, section views, the cursor readout and the receptor check all use the same drawing, so an export always matches the screen.
- **A drawing that cannot be made never takes the app with it.** If a drawing fails, runs over its time or memory budget, or its worker crashes:
  - the calculated grid stays on screen with a note in the panel: "Contours couldn't be drawn for this map. Showing the calculated grid. Details saved.";
  - the worker restarts;
  - the inputs are saved to a small file, and "Show details" opens it, so the problem can be reproduced exactly.

## Changes
- **Rectangular buildings and barriers no longer slow the whole calculation.** A building or barrier drawn as a rectangle square to the grid was handed to the calculation as a different kind of object, which the fast compiled engine could not take. - **Façade and break-out sources use the reference engine again.** 0.83 moved sources radiating from a wall onto the compiled engine. Where break-out panes meet at a building's corner, that engine counted some routes that leave through the wall itself, which the reference engine correctly stops. Single routes differed by up to 22 dB; contour levels by at most 0.003 dB, and receptor levels not at all, on every model checked. ## Bug fixes
- **A screening building's drawing direction no longer changes a level.** Over a building whose roof gives two parallel edges, ISO 9613-2's route (7.4.2) was built along the direction the building's walls were drawn in. For a building drawn clockwise its points came out receiver first. A façade pane, a break-out source or a directional source behind it then took its radiation correction toward a point behind itself, as if radiating through its own wall: up to 8 dB low. Ordinary sources were never affected, because the barrier attenuation itself is symmetric. No real project changed: P1922, P2006 and every padel project give the same receptor levels and padel LAFmax results before and after.
- **CRTN: a wall reflects only for the roads it is near.** The opposite-façade correction (CRTN paragraph 26.2) counted a wall within 100 m of any switched-on road as an opposite façade of every road. Switching one road on could raise another road's level, and a project's total was not the sum of its roads. Each road now uses only the walls within 100 m of itself. No real project changed: every project with a single switched-on road is identical, and P1987, with three roads, is unchanged.
- **CRN: far-side reflections no longer depend on which way the site faces.** The opposite-façade correction compares the track's angle of view with each far-side building's. Where the view crossed due east of the receiver, the two could be measured on different turns of the compass and miss each other, and the correction (up to about 0.5 dB) was lost. - **A court's ends and sides no longer depend on the corner its outline starts at.** Every court calculation, and the plan and 3D drawing, took the first edge of the outline as the court's length. ## New features
- **Padel: strikes and panel impacts as two events, each from its own data.** A new LAFmax method, *Strike + panel*, treats the two things a padel court is heard for separately, as ProPG's two measurement positions do:
  - **Ball strikes.** Every in-play position on a 1 m grid. The sound power is fitted so that the 90th percentile over those positions equals the typical LAFmax measured beside the court. ProPG's typical maximum, the 10th percentile of event maxima, is the level 10 % of events exceed.
  - **The ball on the enclosure.** Every glass and mesh panel. The sound power is fitted so that the 90th percentile over the rebound wall's panels equals the typical LAFmax measured behind it.

  Each receptor takes the louder of its loudest strike and its loudest panel impact, never the two added together. The responsible position shows on the plan and in the Inspector. The loudest strike is often not the nearest: strikes beside receptor-facing glass are screened by it.

  The check shows each mechanism reproducing its own position, and what it gives alone at the other position, where the other mechanism should dominate. On the P2003 court: strikes alone give 57.4 dB behind against 62 dB measured, and panel impacts alone give 59.9 dB beside against 70 dB.

  The upper range adds each mechanism's own spread in the data: with ProPG Table 13.26, strikes +15 dB and panel impacts +13 dB.

  The method needs data at both positions; ProPG Tables 13.25 and 13.26 have them. It reproduces the P2003 audit to the second decimal: strike power 99.35 dB, and Haven Lodge first floor 52.99 dB. Courts on the existing methods are unchanged.
- **"Struck panels reflect from their own glass" is a visible setting.** Under Inspector › Padel court › Event details. Off, a struck panel's event is not mirrored by the court's own glass; that was the method before and is still the default. On is a sensitivity: on the P2003 court the panel power is refitted 2.6 dB lower, and panel levels at the receptors change by up to 2.6 dB.
- **Exports say where their numbers came from.** Results' Excel export, the compliance JSON and the padel Excel export now carry a Provenance sheet:
  - the project file and whether it was saved;
  - the calculation run and whether it still matches the model;
  - the acoustic input and calculation fingerprints.

  An export from a model with unsaved changes also saves the model as calculated beside it ("… - model as exported.ap"), so issued figures can be reproduced. Each padel court's basis now lists the LWAFmax and event height its levels actually used.
- **A supported scripting interface.** `auris.api` gives scripts a stable set of functions:
  - open a project read-only;
  - receptor levels;
  - single-event maxima at receptors;
  - the padel comparison;
  - British National Grid conversion;
  - bearings and compass words in AURIS's +y-south model frame.

  docs/scripting.md has a worked example. A script run from standard input, or without an `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard, now calculates in one process with a warning, where it used to crash with BrokenProcessPool.

AURIS used an eighth. Far from the source that still leaves sections metres across, and the ground and screening terms vary across them. Every section is now also no larger than a thirty-second of its distance, or 2 m if that is larger. Sources near the point being calculated, where sections are already small, are split as before and take no longer. On every project in the corpus, receptors are within 0.03 dB of a 1/128 reference, where they were up to 0.28 dB off. Receptors and contour nodes use the same rule, so a node still equals a receptor at its position.

## Bug fixes
- **Vertical area sources with a reflection now calculate.** Since 0.42, a vertical area source (a façade break-out pane, or a padel panel drawn as a vertical source) stopped the calculation with an error whenever one of its paths reflected off a wall. The reflection search handed its wall openings to the vertical-source integration in a form that integration could not read. It now reads both forms. Other source types are unchanged.
- **Vertical area sources are integrated to convergence.** ISO 9613-2 splits an area source into sections no larger than k times their distance to the receiver. That keeps the path to the receiver representative, but a vertical source also spans heights close to the ground and often stands against a screening edge, such as its own wall's top or end. There, the ground and screening terms change across the source on a scale of metres or centimetres, not tens of metres. A 2 m padel panel 100 m away was treated as one section and read up to 2.7 dB low. Each section of a vertical source is now also kept no larger than half its height above the ground (down to 1 m), and half its distance to the nearest screening edge or, for a reflected path, its reflector (down to 0.25 m). On the 52 panels of a padel court, AURIS now agrees with a 3 cm point-by-point reference within 0.3 dB (95 % within 0.1 dB), where it differed by up to 2.8 dB. On P1922's 11 façade break-out panes, receptors move by 0.01 dB at most, and contour levels behind the buildings by up to 1.5 dB (95 % within 0.75 dB), towards the converged values. A sloping road passes exactly through a contour node now and then, and so does every road vertex placed on a whole metre. The two sides differ by 0.1–0.3 dB mid-span and up to about 6 dB at the apex of a bend. A receptor placed exactly on a road line still has no level.
- **The CRN gap along railways is a clear, deliberate band.** CRN Chart 3 starts at 10 m, so AURIS gives no level nearer a track. Each segment stays within a tolerance of its level (0.4 dB at 25 %, 0.8 dB at 50 %, 1.5 dB at 75 %, 2.25 dB at 100 %, never more than 45 % of the band step) and within a distance of where it is drawn (0.6 % of the drawing's size at 25 %, 7 % at 100 %). The calculation places a transition only to its grid nodes, so it stair-steps; Simplify draws it straight, never across a wall, and contours that run beside it lie on it. - Icons follow light and dark. Toolbar, inspector, project, menu, Contours and 3D glyphs are drawn in the current mode's ink when they are painted, so switching appearance re-tints them. Before, an icon kept the grey it was given when it was made, which was 2.3:1 on the dark panels.
- Coloured text keeps its colour in dark mode but is lightened until it reads at 4.5:1. This covers the teal on preset chips and the Saved chip, amber warnings, and green and red outcome colours in the BS 4142 Annex C tonality, uncertainty and scheme assessment tables. Text on a pale chip of its own colour is left as it is.
- Placeholder text in dark mode uses the muted text colour (5.8:1), not half-transparent text (4.0:1).
- The dark-mode error red and information blue are a touch lighter, so error text on a field reads at 4.6:1 (it was 4.3:1).
- Contour sheets and exports stay white paper in dark mode, as before. The controls around them are now dark-correct.
- Light mode looks the same as before.
- **Maximum levels follow an insertion loss, an enclosure or a silencer.** A level correction whose reason is insertion loss, enclosure or silencer now also reduces the source's maximum events (LAFmax), because it reduces every event. A correction with any other reason applies to LAeq only, as before. So does a correction with no reason, which is every correction in projects saved before 0.60, so their maximum levels do not change. Example: a 95 dB LwA compressor with a 105 dB LWAFmax, 40 m away, with a −10 dB correction. LAeq goes from 46.4 to 36.4 dB whatever the reason. LAFmax stays at 56.4 dB with no reason or a scenario reason, and drops to 46.4 dB when the reason is enclosure.
- The planning-report note on a point source inside a building no longer appears for a source whose data you have stated as measured outside the building. The Source data item states the double counting precisely instead.

- **Padel courts: LAFmax method.** Each padel court's Inspector has a LAFmax section with three things: the source data (a one-line provenance summary and its emission basis), the LAFmax method (Worst case of all · Horizontal area · Vertical surfaces · Nearest-impact points) and a check line such as "Reproduces 70.0 dB at 5 m beside ✓ · rear hold-out −5.4 dB". Vertical surfaces put an impact on each glass and mesh panel (full event power at the panel's outer face; a struck panel neither screens nor reflects its own event). Nearest-impact points are an in-play ring 1.75 m inside the boundary at 2.5 m spacing. Worst case of all takes the highest single event over every candidate of every representation and court, and Results names what governs. Courts drawn from 0.60 start on Worst case of all; existing courts keep the horizontal area, so their results do not change.
- **Self-consistent calibration.** A court calibrated from a measured LAFmax (ProPG Tables 13.25 and 13.26) reproduces it with every representation: each representation's event sound power is solved at the reference position with its own placement, height, the court's walls, reflections, ground and Cmet = 0. The other position of the record (behind the end) is predicted as a hold-out and its residual shown; a reference shadowed by the court's own glass by more than 5 dB, a derived LWAFmax above 105 dB and a BS 4142 impulsivity correction on a DataKustik LAFTeq are flagged.
- **Emission basis.** Measured at reference position(s), Sound power at source, or Apparent sound power including the enclosure. Only the last takes the court's own glass out of the model (and the Glass walls switch is then off), so the glazing is never counted twice. Courts without a stated basis are inferred so results are unchanged (calibrated from a measured level: measured; walls drawn: at source; otherwise: including the enclosure).
- **Padel LAFmax comparison.** From the court's Inspector (Compare at receptors…) or Results › Levels › Maximum levels: per receptor and period, LAeq, LAFmax per representation, the worst case and what governs it (court, representation, event, position, height), the difference from the adopted horizontal area, the internal LAFmax and margin, events above 60 dB outside and 45 dB inside (from the court's play events per hour, an upper bound) and whether the conclusions change; optional height sensitivities (1.0 and 3.0 m) and the record's highest measured event. An editable paragraph marked "consultant to review" states the criteria and their sources, the basis and the double-counting wording, the result, the coincidence of events on several courts and the limitations. Copy for Word and Export Excel.
- **LAFmax origins on the plan.** Selecting a padel court marks each receptor's governing event with ✕ (merged within 2 m for the same court and representation; a receptor stack counts once) and keys the court's glass (screening, or already in the data) and mesh (transparent). Tooltips list the receptors, court, representation, event, height and LWAFmax. A glyph can be dragged; it is kept as user-placed, for display only.
- **Event details.** The statistic (typical maximum, the ProPG 10th percentile of event maxima, or highest measured), the play events per hour with their provenance (feeding the night event counts), and extra events (glass, mesh, voice) only with your own LWAFmax and provenance.
- Results in dark mode: the BS 4142, BS 5228 and Residential outcome pills are soft tints of their colour instead of pale cards, and margins, Stage 1 risks, Element 2, amenity and night-event counts are lightened to 4.5:1 (the green and red margins read at 2.4–2.7:1). The ProPG design statement stays a white page, as it pastes into Word.
- **CRTN night from TRL Method 3 for new roads.** A road drawn or imported from now on takes its night LAeq,8h from its day LA10,18h by the TRL (2006) Method 3 relationship when it is given only an 18-hour flow (Road › Night input › TRL Method 3 · from the 18-hour flow). Before, night used the 18-hour flow, so night LAeq,8h equalled day LAeq,16h. Day levels are unchanged. Roads already in a project keep the night input they were saved with, so existing results are unchanged. TRL Method 3 needs full CRTN propagation: on the ISO 9613-2 route night still uses the 18-hour flow, and Assessment readiness says so.
- **Sound-field conversions on for new projects.** In a new project, BS 4142 and ProPG assess façade receptors at their level less 3 dB (free field), and BS 5228 assesses free-field receptors at their level plus 3 dB (façade). A project saved without this setting keeps it off and keeps its results. Each Results table now states its sound-field basis and whether it converts, for example "free field, façade receptors −3 dB". The Copy Table caption and the Excel basis sheets say the same.
- **The sound-field basis is printed with every Results table.** Levels says whether the receptors are free field, façade, on each method's convention, or vary (then the Sound field column shows each one).
- BS 4142: the band between 0 and +5 dB now reads "Above background, below +5 dB — consider context". The new wording is used in Results, Copy for Word, the report basis, the uncertainty table and Excel.
- BS 5228 ABC: the category now shows the ambient rounded to the nearest 5 dB beside it, for example "A · 65 dB · ambient 60 dB". The rounding itself is unchanged.

## Changes
- **Results has four views instead of six: Levels, BS 4142, BS 5228 and Residential.** Max levels is now part of Levels. Internal and ProPG are now the Residential view. BS 4142 and BS 5228 are unchanged. Nothing has been removed. Every column, setting, button and export from the six modes is still available, and undo works as before. The assessment settings are stored exactly as before, so projects open unchanged. Views saved under the older names open in their new place: Max levels in Levels with maximum levels shown, Internal and ProPG in Residential.
- **Excel report pack: one sheet per view.** Receptor levels now includes the maximum-level columns (once the Max levels sheet), and its basis sheet gives the maximum-level and night event basis. BS 8233 and ProPG replaces the Internal (BS 8233) and ProPG sheets: it has the internal levels and the ProPG columns, and its basis sheet covers both.
- The Copy Table caption names the view, for example "Receptor levels and maximum levels" or "Internal levels (BS 8233) and ProPG (2017) assessment".
- Tooltips and statement text now point to Results › Levels › Maximum levels and Results › Residential.

- The ProPG padel records carry each position's highest measured LAFmax (T13.26: 85 dB beside, 75 dB behind; T13.25: 76 and 66 dB) for the sensitivity row; the 10th percentile stays the governing typical maximum (ProPG Sport and Leisure, June 2026 consultation draft).
- The "highest boundary levels at 5 m" padel preset (LAeq 52 / LAFmax 81 dB) is renamed "Padel court — unverified boundary levels (source not recorded)", marked unverified and listed below the referenced records. Projects that use it keep their values.
- Padel "Worst case of all" is exact but evaluates every candidate position: typical sites take seconds, very large sites (ten or more walled courts and hundreds of receptors) can take several minutes. Horizontal area stays available in the court's LAFmax method menu.
